# Open Mic

> A macOS menu bar app that mixes your microphone with the audio your Mac is
> playing and presents the result as a single virtual microphone, so an app that
> can only read one input hears both sides of a conversation.

Free. macOS 14.2 or later. No account. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized
by Apple. The application source is not published; the landing page and the
released package are.

## What problem it solves

Most AI apps — transcription tools, agents, meeting notes — take a single
microphone input. Your own voice reaches them; the voices your Mac is playing
back do not. Open Mic mixes the two and hands the result to the app as an
ordinary microphone, with no audio routing to configure.

## What people use it for

- Mob programming and pairing with an AI agent: everyone in the room is heard,
  along with whatever the screen is playing, without anyone relaying it.
- Reviewing AI-generated work as a team, without rewriting the discussion into a
  prompt afterwards — the usual friction in AI-driven, AI-native development.
- Turning a whole meeting into AI notes, including the other side of the call.
- Transcribing a conversation as one input rather than two.

## How it works

It installs a Core Audio driver that publishes a virtual input device called
"Open Mic", plus a background service. The app captures the chosen microphone
and the system audio, mixes them, and feeds the driver. You pick "Open Mic" as
the input in whichever app you are using.

## Permissions

Microphone, to capture your voice. Screen Recording, to capture what your Mac is
playing — macOS files system-audio capture under that permission and offers no
narrower one. Open Mic does not capture or record the screen.

## Privacy

Open Mic does not record, store, or upload audio. Mixing happens entirely on the
Mac. How the app you hand the audio to treats it is covered by that service's
own privacy policy.

## Known limitation

Audio played by the same browser that is transcribing can arrive much quieter,
because that browser's echo cancellation subtracts what it is playing from what
it captures. Sometimes it still works; sometimes it stops being picked up. If it
does, play the audio in a different browser or app from the one using Open Mic.
This is processing on the receiving side and cannot be disabled from Open Mic.
